clue.text: Skipper's on call, being top manager

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece being on another means it comes after it

parts.note: to call someone is to ring them
a ship's skipper is its master; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A ship's captain, always on the phone, is said to be the boss of the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like part of a business title, but it is the big top, the circus tent.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringmaster runs the show under the big top, the main circus tent.

clue.text: Live on edge

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
the side of something is its edge

explanation.surface: Someone lives a life always on the brink.
explanation.definitionFit: To live somewhere is to dwell or have one's home there.

clue.text: Subtle meaning is absent from pest

indicators.note: the word is is missing from the word for pest, so its letters are taken out

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: A sly hint goes missing from an annoying person's remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine shade or gradation of meaning, as in tone or expression.

clue.text: Boxer perhaps finds me absent, upset about end of career

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the single letter picked from career
the words finds me absent are knocked over into a new order
the end of career is its final letter

explanation.surface: A boxer fails to find someone and is distressed at the close of their fighting days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter, but it is the dog breed. 'upset' turns FINDSMEABSENT into MANSBESTFIEND, and 'about' puts it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is a breed of dog, and the dog is proverbially the best companion of humankind.

clue.text: Some dinosaurs had these weapons

definitions.meaning: Tyrannosaurus rex famously had tiny forelimbs
firearms carried in the hand, such as pistols and rifles

explanation.surface: A museum label claims certain dinosaurs were armed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: some dinosaurs had little front legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Small arms is the military term for handheld guns; read literally it describes the stubby forelimbs of T. rex.

clue.text: Old Bill is spot on

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a bill in parliament becomes an act

explanation.surface: The police are said to be bang on target.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Bill is British slang for the police, but here the two words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spot on is precisely right, with no error at all.

clue.text: Expedition ignoring a fine outfit

indicators.note: the letters for a and fine are left out of the word for expedition

parts.note: a safari is an expedition, usually to see wildlife
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A traveller skips paying a penalty on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A long draped garment worn as a complete outfit by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Dines out after a turn, having worried greatly

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the pieces from a turn

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

indicators.note: dines out suggests eating at a restaurant, but out signals the letters of dines rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eats at a restaurant after a walk, having fretted a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonised means having suffered great anguish or worry over something.

clue.text: Brainwaves generated by popular tourist attractions

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
sights are places tourists go to see

explanation.surface: Bright ideas come from visiting well-loved landmarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden flashes of understanding or perception, close to bright ideas.

clue.text: Positive associate of Freud has left European city

parts.note: concrete means definite or positive, as in concrete evidence
Carl Jung, the Swiss psychiatrist, worked with Freud

explanation.surface: A confident colleague of Freud has departed a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has left European city' reads as leaving a place, but 'left' and 'European' each give one letter and 'city' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissive term for a harsh urban area of tower blocks and few green spaces.

clue.text: Bridge crossing international state

indicators.note: the word for bridge stretches across the single letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to span a gap is to bridge it

explanation.surface: A bridge spanning a border links two nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a sovereign nation, and a nation is a state.

clue.text: A record, in a sense, must be equivalent

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces sits inside the second pair

parts.note: nous is common sense or gumption
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: An entry in a register should, in a way, be the same as another.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous means comparable or corresponding in some respect, close to equivalent.

clue.text: No resistance in weirdly credible measure taken against racket

indicators.note: the remaining letters are arranged in an odd new order
no resistance means the letter for resistance is removed from the word credible

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: An implausible tale about a tennis racket that shows no resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests tennis, but it means din. 'No' drops R from CREDIBLE, leaving CEDIBLE, which 'weirdly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The decibel is the unit used to measure loudness, so noise is gauged with it.

clue.text: Coarse material seeing nervous response in front of ruler

indicators.note: the twitch comes before the monarch in the answer

parts.note: a tic is a nervous twitch
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch twitches anxiously while wearing rough cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticking is a strong, coarse cotton or linen fabric used to cover mattresses.

clue.text: Alienation of odd people adopted by sect regularly

indicators.note: the odd people are taken inside the letters from the sect
every other letter of sect is taken

parts.note: strange means odd
men can mean people in general

explanation.surface: Peculiar folk taken in by a cult end up cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the 2nd and 4th letters of sect, E and T, which 'adopted by' places around STRANGEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangement is the state of being alienated or separated from others.

clue.text: New editor away drinking rum, went to sleep

indicators.note: the letters for new editor take in the word for rum, as if swallowing it

parts.note: rum means odd or strange
off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: A newly appointed editor is out of the office, drinking and dozing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but means odd.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod off is to fall asleep, especially without meaning to.

clue.text: In Scotland, extended university years for Russian, perhaps

parts.note: lang is the Scots word for long
an age is a long period of years

explanation.surface: A Scottish university gives a student extra years to study Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian is one example of a tongue spoken by a people.

clue.text: Shelled beans found in more mature plant

indicators.note: the middle letters sit inside the word for more mature

parts.note: older means more mature

indicators.note: beans with the shell removed loses its outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Podded beans are discovered in a riper plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisonous evergreen shrub with showy pink or white flowers.

clue.text: Unexpectedly as doleful and needing to change

indicators.note: the words as doleful and must be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly feels gloomy and in need of a fresh start.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means suddenly and without warning, which is close to unexpectedly.

clue.text: Raised standard that is right for such a weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word for standard is written upwards, so read in reverse

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: A banner is held aloft, which is the proper thing for such arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a long, slender, two-edged sword used for thrusting.

clue.text: Divulged information about origin of physics particle

indicators.note: the phrase for divulged information goes round the letter picked from physics

parts.note: to let on is to reveal a secret

indicators.note: the origin of physics is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone leaked details about how physics began.
explanation.definitionFit: A lepton is a subatomic particle such as the electron or neutrino.

clue.text: Coin oddly found in unusually large white flower?

definitions.note: something that flows and is white; the question mark flags the pun on flower

indicators.note: the picked letters sit inside the rearranged ones
the letters of large are put in an unusual order
the odd-numbered letters of coin are taken

explanation.surface: A coin turns up inside a strangely large white bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' looks like a bloom, but it means a thing that flows. 'oddly' gives CI, which 'found in' places in GLAER, the anagram of LARGE from 'unusually'.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacier is a slow-moving river of ice, so a white thing that flows.

clue.text: In Madeira it always includes this side order

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of words Madeira it always

explanation.surface: A diner on Madeira always orders the same side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoghurt and cucumber dish served on the side with Indian food.

clue.text: Copy European drug smuggler importing a source of this

indicators.note: the courier takes the other letters inside, as smuggled goods

parts.note: a mule is someone who carries drugs across borders

indicators.note: the source of this is its first letter

explanation.surface: A European trafficker brings in some contraband, copying others.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to imitate them, often trying to match or surpass them.

clue.text: Instruction for player with worker in love

parts.note: and can mean with, as in fish and chips
an ant is a worker in a colony
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A musician has fallen for a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests a sportsman or actor, but here it is a musician reading a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a tempo marking on sheet music telling a musician to play at a moderate pace.

clue.text: Flash Gordon's first material for dressing

indicators.note: the first letter of the word Gordon is taken

parts.note: lint is soft fabric used to dress wounds

explanation.surface: Flash Gordon, the comic-strip hero, has his wounds bandaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash Gordon' is the space hero, but 'Flash' is the definition and 'Gordon's first' gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: A glint is a brief flash of reflected light.

clue.text: Peer docked in good time

indicators.note: docked means having the tail cut off, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: early means in good time

explanation.surface: A nobleman arrives at the harbour ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' could be a verb, to look closely, but here it is a member of the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman, so a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Appliance of press after meaningless talk

indicators.note: the word for press follows the word for meaningless talk

parts.note: waffle is long-winded, empty talk
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A machine for pressing comes up after a lot of empty chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged kitchen device with a grid pattern used to cook batter into waffles.
